mandatory_rules: No evidence claim may be marked active without at least one source reference.
No dose/reference intake/upper limit may be stored without a source reference and population/context.
No contraindication, interaction, or safety stop may be stored without a source reference.
No Vitami recommendation rule may be activated unless it references one or more evidence_claim_ids.
Symptoms alone must not be encoded as proof of a nutrient deficiency.
A product's commercial availability is not evidence of benefit.
If evidence is uncertain or conflicting, the uncertainty must be stored and surfaced to the user when material.
Source title, organization, URL/identifier, publication/update date when known, access date, and supported claim must be recorded.
Claims intended for EU-facing user interfaces should record EU health-claim status when applicable.
Any automatic dosage adjustment must have an explicit evidence-backed formula/rule; otherwise dosage remains reference-only or requires professional review.
Every material scientific, safety, or regulatory criterion used in a user-facing result must display the actual source used, with a direct original-document link.
Source attribution must identify what the source supports and must not imply endorsement, certification, sponsorship, or partnership with Vitami.
Official logos may be displayed only after checking brand guidelines and permission/reuse conditions; otherwise display the organization name as text.
Distinguish binding legal requirements, regulator scientific opinions, government evidence summaries, clinical guidelines, systematic reviews, and individual studies.
Each claim must be specific to the ingredient, form/preparation, indication/outcome, population, dose context, and duration where relevant.
Record publication/update date and access/review date when available; flag sources whose currency has not been checked.
GRADE is used to assess certainty of evidence and strength of recommendations; PRISMA is used to report systematic reviews and is not a quality score.
Do not activate a claim or recommendation merely because an authoritative organization or database is listed; the specific document must support the specific claim.
preferred_source_order: Individual peer-reviewed studies when higher-level evidence is unavailable

logo_and_attribution_policy.logos: Only after checking brand guidelines and permission; use name-only attribution by default.
logo_and_attribution_policy.endorsement_disclaimer: Attribution identifies information provenance and does not mean the organization endorses Vitami.
